children: Consensus expectations for Marks & Spencer's profit figures might come down ahead of the U.K. retailer's first-half earnings on Nov. 4, Bernstein analysts write. They cite a weak clothing market and delays to cost benefits into the second half of the year as reasons why investors may cool on estimates. "Automation improvements at clothing distribution centers are expected this year, but their benefits will be mainly in 2H," the analysts say. Bernstein has an outperform rating on the stock and a price target of 440 pence. Shares are down 1.9% at 364.10 pence, leading the FTSE 100 index fallers, but are up 10% over the year to date. (joseph.wilkins@wsj.com)
